NOC.thesis_one_line: America's B-21 bomber and Sentinel missile builder, with record orders and steady cash, priced fairly but hurt by repeat cost overruns on fixed-price work.
kill_criteria: Segment operating margin (consolidated, press-release "Segment operating margin rate") below 9.5% in any quarter of H2 2026, versus 10.6% in Q2'26.
FY2026 adjusted free cash flow guidance cut below the $3,100m low end, or FY2026 actual below $3,000m.
A new reach-forward loss or aggregate unfavorable EAC charge of $250m or more on a single program in any quarter (B-21, Sentinel, SiAW, GEM 63XL).
Resolution of the DCMA/DOJ CAS-pension matter with a disclosed charge above $500m, or cost-disallowance applied to future billings.
Net debt/EBITDA (consolidated) above 3.0x, or no share repurchases by Q2 2027 despite positive FCF.
key_adverse_facts: Q2'26 segment operating margin 10.6% vs 11.8%; unfavorable EAC charges of $91m (GEM 63XL) and $68m (SiAW) in Q2'26, GEM 63XL $162m in H1'26; B-21 remaining loss accrual $1.0bn (10-Q 0001133421-26-000034).
2026 MTM-adjusted EPS guide raised $1.20 while segment operating income guidance unchanged at $4,850-$5,000m: raise is tax/other-income driven (Q2'26 tax rate 6.3% vs 17.7%).
DOJ criminal inquiry closed 2026-05-20 but DOJ civil investigative demand and DCMA CAS-pension inquiry remain open; 10-Q says outcome could have a material adverse effect, range not estimable.
Share buybacks paused: $68m in H1'26 vs $1,624m in FY2025; H1 free cash flow negative $(845)m.
data_conflicts: d4 beta -0.11 is unusable for cost of equity.
d4 TTM FCF yield 3.4% vs 2026 guide-midpoint FCF $3.3bn = 4.6% of market cap (seasonality: Q4'25 FCF $3,235m of FY $3,307m).
Next earnings 2026-10-20 from d4 calendar, not confirmed by a filing I opened.
NOC.confidence_in_thesis: medium: backlog and budget demand are documented, but fixed-price execution and a tax-driven EPS raise cap conviction

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for NOC. Reverse DCF at 8% cost of equity implies ~3.8% 10-year FCF growth vs my 6.5% base.

NOC.scenario_basis: Start MTM-adj EPS $28.85 (2026 guide midpoint), growth 1%/6%/9%, exit P/E 14x/17x/19x, dividends $9.88 growing 3%/6%/7%; px $510.52.

MET.thesis_one_line: America's largest employer-benefits and pension insurer, growing in every segment and buying back about 4% of its shares a year at under ten times earnings.
kill_criteria: Adjusted ROE (MetLife, Inc. consolidated, earnings release) below 14.0% for two consecutive quarters (vs 17.0% in Q1 and Q2'26).
Holding-company cash and liquid assets below $3.0bn at any quarter-end, or the combined NAIC RBC ratio below 360%.
Adjusted EPS (ex-notables) growth below +5% YoY for two consecutive quarters, or FY2026 direct expense ratio above 12.1%.
Group Benefits adjusted earnings below $400m in any quarter (vs $503m Q2'26; $401m Q2'25).
Aggregate reasonably possible litigation loss above accrual exceeding $500m (vs $0-$125m at 2026-06-30).
key_adverse_facts: TTM GAAP EPS $5.22 vs adjusted ~$9.71 (54%); adjusted earnings exclude FY2025 net derivative losses $(1,939)m and investment losses $(1,145)m pre-tax.
Q2'26 variable investment income ~$231m pre-tax vs $400m quarterly target (pre-announced in 8-K 0001099219-26-000045); Group Benefits adjusted earnings +25% leans on favorable underwriting.
Unrealized investment losses $(18,677)m net of tax in equity; commercial mortgages $39.6bn (office $14.7bn at 83% LTV); US statutory adjusted capital ~$16.4bn at 6/30/26 vs ~$17.2bn at 12/31/25.
NY False Claims Act qui tam (Total Asset Recovery Services) survived motion to dismiss on 2024-10-13; aggregate reasonably possible loss $0-$125m over accruals.
data_conflicts: d4/triage FCF yield -33.7% and FCF -$21.0bn, total debt $50.3bn are not meaningful; 10-Q consolidated debt ~$20.1bn (short-term 460 + long-term 14,244 + collateral financing 286 + subordinated 5,144).
b1 FCF/price input is not an insurer metric.
MET.confidence_in_thesis: medium: cheap on adjusted earnings with documented buybacks, but adjusted-vs-GAAP gap and VII/underwriting volatility limit conviction

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for MET. Reverse DCF on distributable earnings (70-80% of adjusted earnings) at 9.5% cost of equity implies -0.4% to +1.4% growth vs my 6% base.

MET.scenario_basis: Start FY26E adjusted EPS $9.89 (consensus), growth 0%/7%/11%, exit P/E 7.5x/9.5x/11x, dividends $2.37 growing 3%/6%/8%; px $97.70.

BEN.thesis_one_line: A global fund manager with record assets, returning to net client inflows and expanding in private markets, trading at about ten times adjusted earnings with a 4% dividend.
kill_criteria: Long-term net flows excluding reinvested distributions (release lines) negative for two consecutive quarters (Jun-26: +$14.3bn = 18.4 less 4.1).
Adjusted operating margin (non-GAAP, release) below 24.0% for two consecutive quarters (vs 28.0% Jun-26).
Investment management fee rate (annualised investment management fees / average AUM) below 40.0 bp (vs ~42.7 bp).
Franklin corporate debt (excluding CIPs) above $3.5bn without an acquisition, or breach of the 3.25x consolidated net leverage covenant.
Western Asset class-action or SEC v. Leech outcome producing a charge above $250m, or Western long-term net outflows above $10bn in a quarter (vs $1.1bn Jun-26).
key_adverse_facts: FY2026 YTD long-term net inflows $63.3bn include $28.9bn, $3.2bn and $4.1bn of reinvested distributions (~$27.1bn excluding them) and, from FY2026, uncalled commitments; FY2025 outflows were $(97.4)bn.
Nine-month FY26 GAAP EPS $1.26 vs adjusted $2.13; add-backs include recurring special termination benefits ($123.4m) and a $100.0m SEC penalty (Western Asset).
Western Asset: class action (amended 2026-03-16, more executives named) and SEC v. Leech pending; Western long-term net outflow $1.1bn in Jun-26 quarter.
AUM growth in Q3 FY26 was $98.0bn market-driven of $109.5bn total; beta 1.57; one-time retention equity and carry awards to top executives (8-K 0000038777-26-000194).
data_conflicts: d4 FCF -$3.0bn (yield -17.8%) and totalDebt $3.57bn conflict with the 10-Q: consolidated OCF is distorted by consolidated investment products (CIP debt $13.3bn non-recourse); corporate debt $2.40bn.
Triage claim of persistent outflows is contradicted by FY2026 flow data (with the reinvestment and definition caveats).
Next earnings ~2026-11-06 from d4, not confirmed by a filing.
BEN.confidence_in_thesis: medium-low: low implied growth and improving margins, but earnings quality and market beta are material

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for BEN. Reverse DCF on 85-90% of adjusted earnings at 10% cost of equity implies ~1.4-2.2% growth vs my 6% base.

BEN.scenario_basis: Start FY26E adjusted EPS $2.85 (nine-month actual $2.13 + Q3 run-rate), growth -4%/6%/11%, exit P/E 8.5x/11x/13x, dividends $1.32 growing 0%/3%/4%; px $33.02.
